**HidrAmazônia** — Hydrological and ecophysiological controls on Amazon forests' responses to drought and flooding.

HidrAmazônia is a French-Brazilian research project studying how groundwater and plant functional traits shape the resilience of Amazonian forests to increasing droughts and floods, using two long-term "super-sites": [**Ducke**](https://ppbio.inpa.gov.br/en/Sites/RFAD) (Manaus, Brazil) and [**Paracou**](https://paracou.cirad.fr/) (Kourou, French Guiana).

HidrAmazônia combines long-term forest and hydrological monitoring, ecophysiological trait measurements, and individual-based forest modelling (**TROLL**) to project how Amazon forest structure, composition, and functioning will respond under future climate and land-use scenarios.

- [Forests and Societies](https://ur-forets-societes.cirad.fr/en) 🇫🇷
- [National Institute of Amazonian Research](https://www.gov.br/inpa/pt-br) 🇧🇷
- [Ecology of the Forest of French Guiana](https://umr-ecofog.cirad.fr/en/) 🇬🇫
- [AMAP Lab](https://amaplab.fr/en/index.php) 🇫🇷
- [Center for Research on Biodiversity and Environment](https://crbe.cnrs.fr/en/) 🇫🇷
- [Federal University of Amazonas](https://ufam.edu.br/) 🇧🇷
